system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period

- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Review of Seller’s SPA Positions & Disclosure Letter vs. Wattlebridge Playbook  
**Project Kestrel – Buy-side Advisory (Wattlebridge Holdings)**

---

### Executive Summary
The Seller’s “FINAL” package **departs from the playbook on every material lever**: cap, thresholds, time limits, fundamental/title regime, fraud carve-out, disclosure framework, buyer-knowledge bar, Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, employee-bonus funding, Ironquay indemnity, tax/IP regime and title evidence.  
The Disclosure Letter confirms the factual gaps (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark payoff, no Ironquay payment proof, bonuses missing from funds flow, title only on internal register).  
**No prior written authority from Amelia Frost exists for any fallback positions.**  
**Recommendation:** Issue a comprehensive mark-up rejecting the “standard” framework and re-anchoring every clause to playbook positions. Do not treat any [STANDARD] tag as agreed.

---

### Detailed Departures & Reasoning

| # | Playbook Position | Seller’s Position / Disclosure | Departure & Risk | Reasoning |
|---|-------------------|-------------------------------|------------------|-----------|
| **1** | **General Cap: 25% / AUD 6M** (20% / AUD 4.8M only with Amelia Frost written authority – **none given**) | Cl. 12.1: **20% / AUD 4.8M** – marked [STANDARD] | **Material.** Seller locks in the fallback as “agreed” without buyer principal approval. | The playbook treats 20% as a conditional concession; using it as the opening anchor cedes AUD 1.2M of protection without authority. |
| **2** | **De minimis AUD 5k; Basket AUD 50k (first-dollar recovery once exceeded)** | Cl. 12.2: **De minimis AUD 25k; Basket AUD 250k (excess-only recovery)** | **Material.** 5× higher de minimis, 5× higher basket, and “excess-only” vs. “first-dollar” shifts ~AUD 200k+ of small claims to buyer. | SaaS deals of this size routinely run 0.1–0.2% de minimis and 0.2–0.25% basket; Seller’s 0.1%/1% is aggressive. |
| **3** | **General Claims Period: 24 months** (18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval – **none given**) | Cl. 12.3/13: **18 months**; “any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise” | **Material.** 6 months less runway; the “applies to all Claims” language attempts to collapse fundamental/title/fraud into the short period. | The playbook’s 24-month baseline reflects the latency of SaaS warranty breaches (IP, data, revenue recognition). |
| **4** | **Fundamental/Title: Separate regime – 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar** | “Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity” | **Critical.** Title/capacity defects (e.g. encumbered shares, no authority) would be capped at AUD 4.8M, time-barred at 18 months, and subject to basket/de minimis/knowledge bars. | Title failure is binary and catastrophic; market practice (and playbook) isolates it from commercial warranty regime. |
| **5** | **Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct: Carved out of ALL caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance. No waiver.** | Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5: **Limitations, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance apply to ALL Claims of any nature.** | **Critical.** Seller seeks to cap/limit/time-bar/waive fraud claims – unenforceable in NSW but creates litigation risk and signals bad faith. | NSW law (and playbook) treats fraud as outside contractual limitations; the clause must expressly carve it out. |
| **6** | **Disclosure: Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register, prudent-search deemed disclosure.** | Sch. 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]: **General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), accounts, statutory registers, public records.** | **Material.** Dumps ~10k+ pages on buyer; “deemed knowledge” of everything in data room/public records used to defeat claims. | Playbook requires granular, page-specific disclosure tied to each warranty; general disclosure is rejected in NSW precedent (e.g. *Idameneo*). |
| **7** | **Buyer Knowledge: Delete blanket exclusions. Any qualifier = named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry. Never excuses title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity.** | Cl. 8.3: **“Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from data room or public records.”** | **Material.** Constructive knowledge via advisers/data room/public records = blanket bar; no named Seller knowledge persons; would bar title/capacity/fraud/indemnity claims. | The clause converts buyer’s diligence into a shield for seller; playbook requires seller’s actual knowledge (named individuals + enquiry) only. |
| **8** | **Bluefen Consent: Effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied BEFORE Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone insufficient.** | Cl. 3/6.3: **Reasonable endeavours; consent “satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent.”** Disclosure [2]: **No final written consent, no evidence conditions satisfied.** | **Material.** 30% revenue customer; change-control conditions (cl. 11.3) unmet. “Delivery of consent” ≠ conditions satisfied; post-completion failure = buyer bears loss. | Playbook treats material customer consent as condition precedent with documented condition satisfaction, not best-endeavours promise. |
| **9** | **Riverlark: Current payout + direct repayment from Completion funds + effective security releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.** | Cl. 2/7: **Release “to be provided following Completion.”** Disclosure [3]: **Facility NOT repaid, NO final discharge.** | **Material.** AUD 3.2M debt + security remains on target post-completion; buyer exposed to enforcement, cross-default, consent fees. | Playbook requires debt-free/cash-free at Completion; post-completion discharge is exceptional and needs ironclad undertaking + principal sign-off. |
| **10** | **Employee Bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420k + triggered on-costs = specific line item or seller-funded. Funds flow must not silently exclude.** | Funds flow: **“DD-005 closing bonuses… not separately itemised.”** Disclosure [5]: **On-costs (payroll tax, super) not stated.** | **Material.** AUD 420k + ~20–25% on-costs = ~AUD 500k+ liability sitting in target post-completion, unfunded, unrepresented in price mechanics. | Silent exclusion = purchase price leakage; playbook demands explicit funding (seller cheque or completion adjustment). |
| **11** | **Ironquay IP: Broaden narrow indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure. AUD 180k not independently verified.** | Cl. 11.1: **Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment.** Disclosure [4]: **AUD 180k open; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment.** | **Material.** Narrow indemnity covers only SOW3 fees; excludes IP ownership, infringement, moral rights, third-party claims. AUD 180k payment unproven. | Playbook requires broad IP indemnity (ownership, non-infringement, clearance) with SOW3 cure as subset; verification of payment is prerequisite. |
| **12** | **Export/Privacy Incident (DD-006): Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty
=== END ADVICE ===
